sections.h2: How big is Jefferson County, Georgia, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Wide open describes Jefferson County: 530 square miles, 526 of them land, and fewer than 30 residents per square mile in 2020. Louisville serves as seat and biggest city, joined by Avera, Stapleton, Wadley and Wrens. The legislature established the county on February 20, 1796, per Wikipedia.

Its neighbors are McDuffie, Richmond, Burke, Emanuel, Johnson, Glascock, Washington and Warren. Streams south of a line running southeast from Stapleton, just below State Route 80, empty into the Upper Ogeechee; the small area north of it belongs to Brier Creek and the Savannah system. A single school district follows the county line. The 2020 census found no urban population at all, and residents' median age stood at 43.4.

People 65 and over make up 22.4% of the county and children 21.3%. QuickFacts lists 5,751 households of 2.58 people, a 21.5% poverty rate, and a bachelor's degree for 13.5% of adults. Employers numbered 326 in 2023, with 4,046 jobs.

sections.h2: What is a Jefferson County house worth, and is the market growing?
sections.html:
Prices are low and the headcount is shrinking. An owned home has a midpoint value of $105,400 for 2020-2024, while 15,011 residents in the mid-2025 estimate is 4.5% below the 2020 base.

In 1980 there were 18,403 residents, and by 2010 there were 16,930. Housing units numbered 7,148 in the 2020 census, 13.7% of them vacant. Sellers mostly compete with other older houses, and one with no delinquent years is easier to place.

sections.h2: How has Jefferson County's population changed since 1900?
sections.html:
Jefferson County reached its largest count in 1920, with 22,602 residents, after growing from 6,111 in 1810 and 18,212 in 1900. Numbers slid to 17,174 by 1970, edged up to 18,403 in 1980, and have declined at every count since: 17,408 in 1990, 17,266 in 2000, 16,930 in 2010 and 15,709 in 2020.

The mid-2025 estimate of 15,011 extends the pattern. QuickFacts also reports that 18.7% of people under 65 have no health insurance, 93.4% of households own a computer and 83.7% subscribe to broadband. Retail sales in 2022 averaged $10,893 a person, and 1,631 nonemployer businesses operated in 2024.

With a shrinking market, base your asking price on recent local sales, since figures from ten years back may mislead. Where buyers are few, tidy paperwork counts for more.

sections.h2: Where do I take Jefferson County tax questions?
sections.html:
Payments and bill questions go to the Tax Commissioner, 736 Peachtree Street, Louisville, GA 30434, telephone (478) 625-7736; the counter opens at 8:30 and closes at 5:00 on weekdays. For the worth of a parcel, call the Tax Assessor at (478) 625-8209.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends bills for land, business equipment, vehicles, mobile homes and timber
  • Board of Tax Assessors: receives returns, homestead forms and appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: its record center supplies warranty deed copies and runs the FANS alerts; the tax site lists the clerk at (478) 625-7922

The county commissioners and the school board decide millage; the Tax Commissioner has no vote.

sections.h2: What happens if I miss the Jefferson County deadline?
sections.html:
Land, buildings and business personal property are generally due on November 15, and a 10% penalty follows after another 90 days. Small homesteaded bills, those under $500, escape it.

After that, levying on the parcel is possible. The office calls it a last resort and would rather collect another way.

  • Mobile and modular homes show April 1 on one county page and May 1 on another, so ask which one governs you
  • The year's mobile home tax must be fully paid before a location permit is issued
  • Vehicle tax follows the owner's birthday

The tax site also mentions a one-time state homestead relief grant shown as a line on bills for owners with an approved exemption. Rentals and homes without an exemption were left out.

sections.h2: How do returns and homestead applications work in Jefferson County?
sections.html:
If you hold taxable property on January 1, file at least one return between January 1 and April 1. Real property returns afterward roll over at last year's value until you acquire more land or build.

Business personal property follows its own rule: form PT-50P is filed annually, and items you have sold must be reported or the tax continues. If you file a return that states a lower value and the assessors decline it, that is where your appeal begins.

  • First-time owners take a copy of the warranty deed along to the Tax Assessor's Office
  • Forms are taken any time, though one arriving after April 1 takes effect a year later
  • An approved exemption lasts until you move, sell or request another kind
  • A denial comes to you in writing, with the right to appeal

When a local exemption is bigger than the State's, the local one prevails. The assessor's office can quote the amounts in force.

sections.h2: How can I appeal a Jefferson County value?
sections.html:
Once a notice of changed value reaches you, mail the Board of Tax Assessors a written appeal. One county page counts 45 days from mailing and another says 30, so follow the notice you hold and file early.

Three arguments are open to you: the property should not be taxed, the value is wrong, or it is out of line with comparable parcels. A complaint about how much tax was levied is not accepted. The assessors review, then answer; a remaining dispute goes to the County Board of Equalization for a hearing, and Superior Court follows. Arbitration substitutes for the board, and the assessors' office explains how to choose it.

sections.h2: Which farm, timber and historic programs apply in Jefferson County?
sections.html:
Active farmland may be assessed at 30% of market value rather than the standard 40%. Conservation use is a second route and values farm, timber, sensitive or transitional land by its present use.

  • Covenant: the owner commits to the Board of Tax Assessors to keep the land in that use for at least 10 years, and applications are due in April
  • Standing timber: untaxed until sold or cut, then taxed at full market value times the millage rate
  • Historic buildings: a register-listed structure and up to two surrounding acres can get preferential treatment

If you own acreage, talk to the assessor before listing so you know what the covenant requires of a new owner.

sections.h2: How do I clear tax before a Jefferson County closing?
sections.html:
Obtain the payoff figure from the Tax Commissioner in writing, then have it paid at the table. A bill older than 90 days already carries the 10% penalty.

The Clerk of Superior Court runs FANS, a free service you join voluntarily that alerts you when records are filed for your property. Sign up before you list, so a lien cannot appear mid-contract. For an inherited or former rental house, ask for each earlier year's balance by itself.

faqs.q: What date are Jefferson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Generally November 15 for land, buildings and business property; 90 days later, a 10% penalty applies.

faqs.q: Which phone reaches the Jefferson County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: (478) 625-7736. The office is at 736 Peachtree Street in Louisville and keeps counter hours from 8:30 to 5:00 on weekdays.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty on a small homesteaded Jefferson County bill?
faqs.a: No. The 90-day penalty skips homesteaded property whose bill is under $500.

faqs.q: Until what date can a Jefferson County owner apply for homestead?
faqs.a: April 1. The office takes applications through the year, though a later one starts a year after.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about value in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Assessor, (478) 625-8209; the Tax Commissioner only bills and collects.
